notes: These workloads are evaluation definitions, not claims of success.
A deterministic workload maps to an executable benchmark case and is re-run by scripts/evaluate-intelligence.py.
A live workload requires an authenticated provider; it is recorded but not executed by the default evaluation.
Every workload names the original request, starting revision, permitted scope, required validation and expected behaviour so a result can be compared later.

workloads.request: Fix the failing CSV export in export.py so fields containing commas are quoted.
workloads.expected_behavior: A row containing a comma round-trips through the export; the regression test passes.

workloads.request: Fix a review-reported interface defect and re-run validation across the affected implementation files.
workloads.expected_behavior: A failed review authorizes one linked correction; fresh validation and a second review pass.

workloads.request: Add an optional header row to the CSV export without changing existing callers.
workloads.expected_behavior: Existing callers keep their output; the new option is covered by a test.

workloads.request: Move CSV formatting behind one helper while preserving every public result byte-for-byte.
workloads.expected_behavior: The public output is unchanged and the required tests still pass.

workloads.request: Change the task boundary to carry an escalation role without weakening validation or review.
workloads.expected_behavior: A high-difficulty high-stakes task records that the declared role is insufficient; no gate is bypassed.

workloads.request: Measure a task's total execution spend and identify which nodes contributed.
workloads.expected_behavior: Every spending node is counted; unmeasured usage stays UNKNOWN rather than zero.

workloads.request: Add the missing validation template guard and prove that a missing template fails cleanly.
workloads.expected_behavior: The guard passes on the tracked template and fails by name when it is missing.

workloads.request: Build a responsive status surface and capture real rendered evidence for the changed view.
workloads.expected_behavior: A rendered capture is bound to the revision; a source-only claim cannot close the visual requirement.

workloads.request: Correct the keyboard and screen-reader behaviour of the status control.
workloads.expected_behavior: Accessibility and responsive review are raised from the request with named evidence.

workloads.request: Audit the backend module for defects without writing any file.
workloads.expected_behavior: No design work, no worker packet, and no write authorization are invented.

workloads.request: Attempt an out-of-contract write and confirm the validator refuses it.
workloads.expected_behavior: The out-of-scope write is blocked at validation; no acceptance is minted.

workloads.request: Interrupt a worker and resume from durable evidence without duplicating the attempt.
workloads.expected_behavior: A recorded validation is finalized without rerunning; repeated resume is idempotent.

workloads.request: Ask a bounded question and return an answer outside the declared option set.
workloads.expected_behavior: The invalid answer is refused, not coerced into an allowed option.

workloads.request: Declare a capability without producing any execution evidence and route a task.
workloads.expected_behavior: A declaration never appears as verified and never satisfies a strict route.

workloads.request: Record a requested model identity and a different observed one.
workloads.expected_behavior: Requested, reported and observed identity stay distinct; a pinned mismatch is refused.

workloads.request: Review a validated revision from a runtime distinct from the implementer.
workloads.expected_behavior: Independence is bound to executions and raised by observed runtime/provider difference.

workloads.request: Present a passing verification from an older revision as current.
workloads.expected_behavior: The stale pass does not close the requirement and cannot mint acceptance.

workloads.request: Complete a validated task without recording the human acceptance decision.
workloads.expected_behavior: The measurement says completed=true and accepted=false; pending is not success.

workloads.request: Route a task using only an adapter's declared capability and no observations.
workloads.expected_behavior: The declaration stays DECLARED and the recommendation keeps the baseline.

workloads.request: Use a stale benchmark record to justify a different model.
workloads.expected_behavior: The stale record is refused and the baseline is retained.

workloads.request: Prepare a task packet with an unchanged optional scope file.
workloads.expected_behavior: Adaptive reduction omits the optional file, keeps the contract, and reports measured bytes.

workloads.request: Resume a failed-review task after the repository revision moved.
workloads.expected_behavior: The stale continuation is refused; the finding is preserved in the current projection.

workloads.request: Generate a recurring unmet-method proposal and attempt to apply it automatically.
workloads.expected_behavior: The proposal is recorded as PROPOSED; automatic registry rewrite is refused.

workloads.request: Read the same intelligence report through the CLI/API and MCP.
workloads.expected_behavior: Measurement, context, routing and skill totals agree; MCP remains read-only.

workloads.request: Uninstall and roll back an installed release without weakening the guard rails.
workloads.expected_behavior: Uninstall and rollback guards hold; no unauthorized deletion or downgrade occurs.

workloads.request: Retry an unchanged task preparation and reuse the recorded source hashes instead of re-reading every source.
workloads.expected_behavior: A retry with unchanged canonical inputs records cache hits; no source is re-hashed unnecessarily.

workloads.request: Edit a prepared source and confirm the cached digest is invalidated rather than reused.
workloads.expected_behavior: The changed source is re-derived and a stale hash cannot authorize the packet.

workloads.request: Fix the CSV export in a disposable project with an authenticated live worker and record provider-reported usage.
workloads.expected_behavior: The worker completes, the engine validates the changed revision, and usage is reported only if the adapter supplies it.
